content.comment_body: Hello, I'm attempting to set up communication between [product_name] and a [product_name] PLC. My goal is to transmit two words of data—random numbers—to the [product_name], which will display them on an HMI screen so I can confirm success. The [product_name] sends the words back to the PLC, which should then alter the data (for example, by adding 1) and repeat this cycle. I’ve explored manuals about configuring master-slave communication between these devices but haven’t found a clear solution. Can anyone suggest useful resources or methods for achieving this? Thank you in advance, [user_name].
Hello [user_name], You might find this [document] helpful: [url]. Best regards, [user_name]
Hi, Visit [url] for examples using [product_name] with HMI and also with [product_name] PLCs in a concise format. Hope this helps.
Additionally, my [product_name] keeps showing a network error message. I haven't been able to resolve it yet.
Hello, After completing the setup, try sending and receiving some values. Regards, [user_name]
Yes, I’m aware. This isn’t my first time working with [product_name]; I’ve programmed other functions using its I/Os. The network error still occurs—even when the Ethernet cable is unplugged.
Hello, You should review the resources we referenced and consult the [product_name] system manual. Regards, [user_name]

I've followed the manual for communication between [product_name] and PLC, but it still doesn't work. I’m using [product_name] engineering software version [version_no], and when I created a data block, I couldn’t access block options like offset—the column was greyed out and unavailable. Can anyone explain why this is happening?

You need to adjust your data block properties. The issue is that it's an optimized data block, which removes data offsets. Right-click the DB, select Properties, then Attributes, and uncheck 'Optimized block access.'

Do you have HMI access to your [product_name]? There are several settings you must configure correctly, such as IP addresses and subnet masks—both in the [product_name] and on the HMI. Ensure the HMI’s connection settings match the [product_name] IP address. If issues persist, you can send me a private message with your email address for more direct assistance.

This discussion centers on communication issues between [product_name] and [product_name] PLCs. I believe public troubleshooting here can help many users, whereas private help benefits only one. Regards, [user_name]

You’re absolutely right. My intention isn’t to help just one person. I recently started communicating between two [product_name] units and an HMI, so I've learned some troubleshooting tips for connection problems. Sometimes, focusing on specific issues and repeating questions may achieve faster solutions than listing every possible mistake here. When questions are relevant to multiple users, I’ll respond publicly for everyone’s benefit.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are facing challenges when setting up communication between [product_name] and [product_name] PLCs, notably with network settings and engineering software data block configurations. Users report persistent network error messages on [product_name], even when Ethernet is disconnected. Manual instructions for setup often confuse users due to missing or inaccessible data block parameters, often caused by default optimized block settings. There is a need for clearer troubleshooting advice regarding network configuration, device connectivity, and proper software setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want an easy and reliable method to establish communication between [product_name] and [product_name] PLCs, straightforward data block configuration in engineering software, and seamless HMI data display—without frequent network errors or inaccessible settings.
